sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from the uniformly conditioned causal fixed-\(k\) VMW submodel with no separately assumed latent outcome-moment envelope.
sampling_model.units: \(O_i=(T_i,X_i,Z_i,Y_i)\), for \(i=1,\ldots,n\), are independent with common observed law \(P_O\).
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment is binary, and every joint latent-class and treatment-arm probability is at least \(\pi_0\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every joint latent-class and treatment-arm probability is at least \(\pi_0\), and \(A_0,A_1,B\) have smallest singular value at least \(\sigma_0\).  No treatment-effect eigengap is imposed for law-level results; the \(g\)-window is used only for labeled coordinates.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The published VMW boundedness conditions are imposed separately on \(X\), \(ZX^\top\), and \(YZX^\top\). Armwise empirical moments divide by \(\max\{1,N_{t,n}\}\), are zero on empty arms, and combine with \(n^{-1}\sum_iX_i\) to form \(\widehat S_n\). The theoretical route applies Borel nearest-summary projection and \(\overline F\); the computable route minimizes an explicit no-advice finite structured lattice and never diagonalizes the raw empirical operator.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The published structural/finite-regularity model imposes the two proxy conditional independences, causal consistency, armwise latent ignorability, qualitative proxy rank, and strict positivity, but not the fixed quantitative margins used here.  The explicit quotient pair satisfies those base conditions even though its collision point is outside the separated simple-effect recovery class of Theorem 7.2; the labeled pair is separated.

Theorem 5.4 identifies every polynomial latent-effect moment, while Section 7.1 and Theorem 7.2 localize roots and recover weights under separated simple effects with inverse nearest-eigengap dependence; they do not provide the collision-uniform positive-law modulus proved here.
Projection of noisy summaries onto a feasible truncated-moment space guarantees a positive finite mixing measure and yields Wasserstein rates for Gaussian mixture deconvolution.
Around an \(m_0\)-component ordinary mixture fitted with \(m\) components, the local minimax Wasserstein rate is \(n^{-1/(4(m-m_0)+2)}\), whereas pointwise root-\(n\) behavior can occur.
Necessary and sufficient testing-versus-estimation conditions govern honest adaptive Wasserstein confidence sets over density-smoothness classes.
Honest confidence regions may be centered at adaptive estimators, with achievable diameter controlled jointly by estimation and testing rates.
Data-driven inference for Wasserstein distance between topic-model mixing measures handles nonsmooth transport geometry and supplies asymptotically valid confidence intervals for that distance.

body.tldr: On a uniformly conditioned causal VMW submodel, the primary theorem is a gap-free Lipschitz modulus from the observable moment summary to the positive quotient latent-effect law in \(W_1\), uniform through simultaneous effect merges and splits. Root-\(n\) estimation, honest root-\(n\)-diameter confidence sets, and a cluster report with explicit true-cluster association follow from that modulus. Same-class minimax corollaries give root-\(n\) quotient-law risk and effect-ordered weight risk \(\min\{1,(\sqrt n\,\delta)^{-1}\}\), using factorization-preserving pairs on an explicit full-rank unequal-weight two-class witness. Each converse also transfers to any published-VMW comparator class containing its exact two-point witness pair; no containment of an entire local neighborhood is required. The quotient collision point belongs to the published structural/finite-regularity model but lies outside the separated Theorem 7.2 recovery class, whereas the labeled pair is separated. The modulus, estimator uppers, confidence and cluster guarantees, and matching-minimax conclusions remain restricted to the stated uniformly conditioned classes.

project_justification.gap: Virk, Mazaheri, and Wu identify the operator moments and analyze separated eigenpair recovery, but do not give collision-uniform positive-law estimation or an evaluable confidence/report construction when empirical eigenvalues may be nonreal.
project_justification.niche: The regular causal object is the quotient probability law that aggregates mass at equal effects. Effect-ordered weights remain irregular near a collision, while transport over an unresolved cluster can still be root-\(n\).
project_justification.fill: The paper makes the positive-measure \(W_1\) modulus the root theorem on a uniformly conditioned causal VMW submodel, derives total root-\(n\) estimation, honest root-\(n\)-diameter sets and well-posed cluster reports, and calibrates same-class quotient-law and labeled-weight minimax risk using observed-Kullback--Leibler pairs that preserve the proxy factorization.  The lower bounds transfer further to precisely those published-VMW comparator classes containing the corresponding two witness laws; whole-neighborhood containment is unnecessary, while all upper and inference guarantees retain their narrower class scope.

body.related_work: Virk, Mazaheri, and Wu (2026, Theorem 5.4, Proposition 6.2, Assumption 4, and Theorem 7.2) provide the population operator-moment identity and the known homogeneity reduction.  In their fixed-dimensional finite-sample regime, Assumption 4 imposes finite almost-sure envelopes for \(X\), \(ZX^\top\), and \(YZX^\top\), positive marginal treatment-arm probability, and a positive population singular-value margin; its other named constants are derived conditioning quantities.  Theorem 7.2 additionally assumes proxy richness, strict latent positivity, pairwise-distinct treatment effects when \(k\ge2\), and its stated sample-dependent radius conditions before delivering high-probability treatment-effect, anchor-normalized feature-matrix, and simplex-projected mixture-weight recovery.  Their structural/finite-regularity model contains the explicit quotient collision pair because it retains full proxy rank and strict positivity without requiring distinct effects, but the collision point is outside that separated recovery theorem; the labeled witness pair is separated. Consequently, the two Le Cam converses transfer to any published-VMW comparator class containing the corresponding exact pair, with no need for whole-neighborhood containment. The gap-free positive-law modulus, estimator uppers, confidence and cluster guarantees, and matching-minimax conclusions remain on the explicitly narrower uniformly conditioned causal submodel. Mazaheri, Squires, and Uhler (2025) identify a finite latent-effect mixture through scalar synthetic moments and a Hankel pencil, without collision-uniform inference. Bauer and Fike (1960) localize spectra of perturbed diagonalizable operators, while Kato (1995, Chapter II) supplies contour-defined aggregate projectors for externally isolated clusters; neither result assigns positive causal spectral masses through a merge. Wu and Yang (2020, Sections 1, 4, and 5) project noisy summaries onto a feasible moment space before positive atomic extraction in Gaussian mixture deconvolution and inform the repair handle. Heinrich and Kahn (2018, Sections 3--5) and Ho and Nguyen (2016) analyze collision singularities for ordinary mixtures, not factorization-preserving pairs in the VMW observed proxy experiment. Deo and Randrianarisoa (2023), Robins and van der Vaart (2006), and Bing, Bunea, and Niles-Weed (2025) inform the confidence-set architecture but do not treat multiplicity of a nonnormal causal operator. Miao, Geng, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2018) motivate proxy conditional-independence and rank discipline. Van Amsterdam et al. (2022) provide the PROTECT stage-III NSCLC consumer, conditional on a separate finite-fitness and censoring bridge; their hazard model is not claimed to lie in \(\mathcal M\). Brown and Purves (1973) supply the measurable-extrema selection theorem used to choose a Borel nearest point in the compact feasible-summary closure.
body.interpretation: The regular inferential object is the quotient law, not an effect-ordered labeling of latent classes. When effects collide, the lattice estimator and Wasserstein confidence sets continue to operate at root-\(n\) scale. The cluster report merges coordinates unresolved at radius \(R_{n,\alpha}/m_\star\) and reports their aggregate mass; only externally separated clusters receive sharper coordinate interpretation. The theoretical image set and computable outer set are both honest but are not asserted equal or nested.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The analytic collision bottleneck is settled by the gap-free positive-measure modulus, including simultaneous merges and splits and nonreal raw empirical spectra after feasible-summary projection. The explicit factorization-preserving calculations also settle the two local lower-bound orders. The remaining open issue is computational rather than statistical: nearest projection and exact inversion of the continuum feasible-summary set may be expensive, and \(\mathrm{oeq:constructive\text{-}total\text{-}repair}\) asks whether the original sharp summary-inversion image can be computed exactly in polynomial time in the fixed-dimensional exact-real model. The finite-library net estimator supplies a polynomial-time root-\(n\) law estimator, but does not by itself compute that exact sharp image.
body.honest_scope: The law-level theorems fix and know \(k,d_x,d_z\), use the exact VMW observable conditional independences, and impose two explicitly new uniform-conditioning conditions: a lower bound on every joint latent-arm probability and singular-value margins for \(A_0,A_1,B\). These conditions imply \(P(T=t)\ge k\pi_0\) and, under the conditional normalization of \(M_t(P)\), \(\sigma_k(M_t(P))\ge\pi_0\sigma_0^2\); the converse inclusion and gap-free resolution of the full VMW class are not claimed. The displayed potential-outcome and effect envelopes are derived from the retained proxy rank, observable envelopes, separation, consistency, armwise ignorability, and latent--arm positivity conditions; no separate compact-support assumption is imposed. The two-sided \(g\)-window is an additional local-regime shell used only for labeled weights. Population identification and the homogeneous identities \(\Delta Q(P)=\tau_\star I_k\) and \(\nu_P=\delta_{\tau_\star}\) are published VMW background. Each lower bound transfers to any published-VMW comparator class containing its exact two-point witness pair, but no whole-neighborhood containment is required and no gap-free modulus, estimator upper, confidence, cluster, or matching-minimax result transfers with it. The quotient collision point is in the published structural/finite-regularity model but outside the separated Theorem 7.2 recovery class; the labeled pair is separated. Recovery of latent labels at equality, unknown \(k\), and exact polynomial-time computation of the sharp summary-inversion image remain outside the settled scope. PROTECT remains a conditional consumer until a separate theorem maps a prespecified finite fitness stratification and bounded censoring-adjusted outcome into the VMW moment model.
